# googleplay_one_time_product (Resource)

A one-time product of an app (a product bought or rented once, as opposed to a subscription), with its listings, its tax settings and its purchase options and their regional prices. It uses the `monetization.onetimeproducts` API, not the deprecated `inappproducts`.

Purchase options are part of this resource because the API creates and edits them by updating the product. The resource is authoritative for them: one that exists in Play Console and not in the configuration is planned for deletion.

~> **A product id is reserved forever**, even after the product is deleted.

Offers on a purchase option (pre-orders, discounts) are not managed yet. Deleting a purchase option that has offers fails until the offers are removed in Play Console.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "googleplay_one_time_product" "remove_ads" {
  package_name = "com.example.app"
  product_id   = "remove_ads"

  listings = {
    "en-US" = {
      title       = "Remove ads"
      description = "Removes every ad from the app, for good."
    }
  }

  purchase_options = {
    # A new purchase option is a draft until its state says otherwise.
    standard = {
      state = "ACTIVE"

      # A plain purchase. Use `rent = { rental_period = "P30D" }` for a rental.
      buy = {
        legacy_compatible = true
      }

      regional_configs = {
        US = {
          price = { currency_code = "USD", amount = "9.99" }
        }
        GB = {
          price = { currency_code = "GBP", amount = "8.99" }
        }
        JP = {
          price = { currency_code = "JPY", amount = "1500" }
        }
      }

      # Prices for any region Google Play launches in later.
      new_regions_config = {
        usd_price = { currency_code = "USD", amount = "9.99" }
        eur_price = { currency_code = "EUR", amount = "9.49" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `listings` (Attributes Map) The store listing of the product by BCP-47 language code, for example `en-US`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--listings))
- `package_name` (String) The package name (application id) of the app, for example `com.example.app`. The app must already exist in Play Console: the API cannot create one. Changing it creates a new product.
- `product_id` (String) The product id of the one-time product, unique within the app: lower-case letters, digits, underscores and dots, starting with a letter or digit, at most 40 characters. **A product id is reserved forever**, even after the one-time product is deleted, so it cannot be reused. Changing it creates a new one-time product.
- `purchase_options` (Attributes Map) The purchase options of the product by purchase option id: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, at most 63 characters. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--purchase_options))

### Optional

- `latency_tolerance` (String) How quickly a change must reach clients: `PRODUCT_UPDATE_LATENCY_TOLERANCE_LATENCY_SENSITIVE` (within minutes; at most 7,200 updates per app per hour) or `PRODUCT_UPDATE_LATENCY_TOLERANCE_LATENCY_TOLERANT` (within 24 hours; a far higher quota). It is sent with every call that accepts it. Left out, the API uses latency-sensitive. It is a setting of the request, not of the product: changing it alone calls nothing.
- `offer_tags` (Set of String) Up to 20 custom tags for this product, returned to the app by the billing library. Each is lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, at most 20 characters.
- `regions_version` (String) The version of Google Play's list of available regions that the regional prices in this configuration are written against. The API requires it on every call that creates or changes the product, and accepts an older version than the current one. Defaults to `2022/02`. Google publishes the current version in [this article](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10532353), and the `googleplay_converted_region_prices` data source reports it as `region_version`. The value in state is what the configuration says, not the version the API reports the product was last written with.
- `restricted_payment_countries` (Set of String) Region codes of the countries where the purchase is restricted to payment methods registered in the same country. Left out, there is no restriction.
- `tax_and_compliance_settings` (Attributes) Tax and legal compliance settings. Left out, the settings Google Play assigns are read back and kept. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tax_and_compliance_settings))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `{package_name}/{product_id}`.

<a id="nestedatt--listings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `listings`

Required:

- `description` (String) The description of the product in this language. At most 200 characters.
- `title` (String) The title of the product in this language. At most 55 characters.


<a id="nestedatt--purchase_options"></a>
### Nested Schema for `purchase_options`

Optional:

- `buy` (Attributes) Makes this a purchase option that is bought. Exactly one of `buy` and `rent` must be set; write `buy = {}` for a plain purchase. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--purchase_options--buy))
- `new_regions_config` (Attributes) The prices to use in any region Google Play launches in later. Left out, the purchase option is not made available in new regions automatically. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--purchase_options--new_regions_config))
- `offer_tags` (Set of String) Up to 20 custom tags for this purchase option, returned to the app by the billing library. Each is lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, at most 20 characters.
- `regional_configs` (Attributes Map) The price and availability of the purchase option by region code, for example `US`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--purchase_options--regional_configs))
- `rent` (Attributes) Makes this a purchase option that is rented. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--purchase_options--rent))
- `state` (String) The state of the purchase option: `DRAFT`, `ACTIVE` or `INACTIVE`. A new purchase option is a draft until activated. Set `ACTIVE` to make it available and `INACTIVE` to retire it; the provider reaches the state with the `purchaseOptions.batchUpdateStates` call. A purchase option that has left `DRAFT` cannot return to it. Left out, the state is whatever the API reports and is never changed.
- `withdrawal_right_type` (String) The classification of the product for users in regions with a right of withdrawal: `WITHDRAWAL_RIGHT_DIGITAL_CONTENT`, `WITHDRAWAL_RIGHT_SERVICE`. The API defaults to `WITHDRAWAL_RIGHT_DIGITAL_CONTENT`.

<a id="nestedatt--purchase_options--buy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `purchase_options.buy`

Optional:

- `legacy_compatible` (Boolean) Whether the purchase option is available to billing flows that predate the one-time products model. At most one buy option of a product can be. Defaults to `false`.
- `multi_quantity_enabled` (Boolean) Whether a buyer can purchase more than one in a single checkout. Defaults to `false`.


<a id="nestedatt--purchase_options--new_regions_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `purchase_options.new_regions_config`

Required:

- `eur_price` (Attributes) The price in EUR for new regions. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--purchase_options--new_regions_config--eur_price))
- `usd_price` (Attributes) The price in USD for new regions. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--purchase_options--new_regions_config--usd_price))

Optional:

- `availability` (String) Whether the prices are used for new regions: `AVAILABLE`, `NO_LONGER_AVAILABLE`. Defaults to `AVAILABLE`.

<a id="nestedatt--purchase_options--new_regions_config--eur_price"></a>
### Nested Schema for `purchase_options.new_regions_config.eur_price`

Required:

- `amount` (String) The amount as a decimal string, for example `"4.99"`. It is converted to the API's units and nanos exactly, never through a floating-point number, and `"4.50"` and `"4.5"` are the same amount. At most 9 fractional digits.
- `currency_code` (String) The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, for example `USD`.


<a id="nestedatt--purchase_options--new_regions_config--usd_price"></a>
### Nested Schema for `purchase_options.new_regions_config.usd_price`

Required:

- `amount` (String) The amount as a decimal string, for example `"4.99"`. It is converted to the API's units and nanos exactly, never through a floating-point number, and `"4.50"` and `"4.5"` are the same amount. At most 9 fractional digits.
- `currency_code` (String) The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, for example `USD`.



<a id="nestedatt--purchase_options--regional_configs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `purchase_options.regional_configs`

Optional:

- `availability` (String) The availability of the purchase option in the region: `AVAILABLE`, `NO_LONGER_AVAILABLE`, `AVAILABLE_IF_RELEASED`, `AVAILABLE_FOR_OFFERS_ONLY`. `NO_LONGER_AVAILABLE` is only accepted for a region that was `AVAILABLE` before. Defaults to `AVAILABLE`.
- `price` (Attributes) The price in the region, in the currency Google Play links to the region. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--purchase_options--regional_configs--price))

<a id="nestedatt--purchase_options--regional_configs--price"></a>
### Nested Schema for `purchase_options.regional_configs.price`

Required:

- `amount` (String) The amount as a decimal string, for example `"4.99"`. It is converted to the API's units and nanos exactly, never through a floating-point number, and `"4.50"` and `"4.5"` are the same amount. At most 9 fractional digits.
- `currency_code` (String) The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, for example `USD`.



<a id="nestedatt--purchase_options--rent"></a>
### Nested Schema for `purchase_options.rent`

Required:

- `rental_period` (String) How long the user has the entitlement, from the purchase, as an ISO 8601 duration such as `P30D`.

Optional:

- `expiration_period` (String) How long the user has, after starting to consume the entitlement, before it is revoked, as an ISO 8601 duration.



<a id="nestedatt--tax_and_compliance_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tax_and_compliance_settings`

Optional:

- `is_tokenized_digital_asset` (Boolean) Whether the product is declared as a product representing a tokenized digital asset. Defaults to `false`.
- `product_age_rating_tier_by_region_code` (Map of String) The age rating tier of the product by region code. The API currently supports only the region `US`. Each value is one of: `PRODUCT_AGE_RATING_TIER_EVERYONE`, `PRODUCT_AGE_RATING_TIER_THIRTEEN_AND_ABOVE`, `PRODUCT_AGE_RATING_TIER_SIXTEEN_AND_ABOVE`, `PRODUCT_AGE_RATING_TIER_EIGHTEEN_AND_ABOVE`.
- `product_tax_category_code` (String) The product tax category code, which decides the transaction tax rates applied.
- `regional_tax_configs` (Attributes Map) Tax configuration by region code. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tax_and_compliance_settings--regional_tax_configs))

<a id="nestedatt--tax_and_compliance_settings--regional_tax_configs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tax_and_compliance_settings.regional_tax_configs`

Optional:

- `eligible_for_streaming_service_tax_rate` (Boolean) Whether the product is a streaming product, for US state and local sales tax. Only supported in the United States. Defaults to `false`.
- `streaming_tax_type` (String) The tax category for communications or amusement taxes in the United States: `STREAMING_TAX_TYPE_TELCO_VIDEO_RENTAL`, `STREAMING_TAX_TYPE_TELCO_VIDEO_SALES`, `STREAMING_TAX_TYPE_TELCO_VIDEO_MULTI_CHANNEL`, `STREAMING_TAX_TYPE_TELCO_AUDIO_RENTAL`, `STREAMING_TAX_TYPE_TELCO_AUDIO_SALES`, `STREAMING_TAX_TYPE_TELCO_AUDIO_MULTI_CHANNEL`.
- `tax_tier` (String) The tax tier for a reduced tax rate: `TAX_TIER_BOOKS_1`, `TAX_TIER_NEWS_1`, `TAX_TIER_NEWS_2`, `TAX_TIER_MUSIC_OR_AUDIO_1`, `TAX_TIER_LIVE_OR_BROADCAST_1`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = googleplay_one_time_product.remove_ads
  id = "com.example.app/remove_ads"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a one-time product, with its purchase options, by package name and product id.
tofu import googleplay_one_time_product.remove_ads com.example.app/remove_ads
```
